clue.text: Pill one must take on one's rounds

definitions.text: Pill one must take on one's rounds

parts.words: Pill one must take on one's rounds
parts.note: reads like medicine to be taken while a doctor does the rounds, but pill is slang for a small sphere, and rounds are trips over eighteen holes

explanation.surface: A patient is told which tablet to swallow during the day's visits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pill is old slang for a ball, and a golfer carries this one round the course.

clue.text: As expected, lost at sea, with one female missing

indicators.note: missing says one letter is absent from the phrase for lost at sea

parts.note: a ship lost at sea has gone off course
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A ship has gone astray and, predictably, one woman is unaccounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops one of the two Fs from OFF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning naturally or as anyone would expect.

clue.text: Grim pro calling one or two clubs, say

parts.note: pro means in favour of, i.e. for

parts.words: calling one or two clubs, say
parts.note: in the card game bridge, calling 'one club' or 'two clubs' is making a bid

explanation.surface: A golf professional sounds stern while choosing which clubs to use.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a golf pro picking clubs; really 'clubs' is the card suit in bridge, where a call is a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a grim, stern look is a menacing, unfriendly one.

clue.text: European entertains a learner from Commonwealth

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an Austrian is a European
L is the learner-driver abbreviation

explanation.surface: A continental host welcomes a student from one of the former British territories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' is the container signal: the nationality takes in the two short pieces as a host takes in guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a member of the Commonwealth of Nations, so its people come from that association.

clue.text: Possibly right kind of thinking

definitions.meaning: right is one example of a side, and an adjective for 'to the side' covers it
the phrase for creative, sideways problem-solving uses this adjective

explanation.definitionFit: The word means 'to the side', and in another sense names indirect, creative thinking.

clue.text: Second vehicle 9 had to face

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A second car crashes, and someone has to face the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is Al Capone, nicknamed Scarface for the mark on his cheek, so the definition reads 'what 9 had to (his) face'.
explanation.definitionFit: Capone's facial wound gave him his nickname, so the mark he had on his face is this.

clue.text: Shook a hand, holding this pipe

indicators.note: holding says the run of letters is held within the words Shook a hand

explanation.surface: Someone shook another person's hand while clutching a water pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of oriental water pipe, smoked through a long tube.

clue.text: State banks are ruined

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Across the country, financial institutions have collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a US state in the Great Plains.

clue.text: Gangster single-handedly carrying explosive device

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: doing something single-handedly is doing it alone
a cap is a small explosive charge, as in a cap gun

explanation.surface: A mobster, working by himself, is armed with a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: A cap is the small charge fired in a toy cap gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the notorious Chicago mobster of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: Sun caused this high-flier's downfall

parts.note: reads like a tabloid newspaper ruining a celebrity, but describes the Greek youth whose wax wings melted when he flew too close to the sun

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper brought about the fall of a prominent figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, which is the surface's false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth he flew too near the sun on wings of wax and feathers and fell into the sea.

clue.text: It's decisive in court in case of six of one and half-a-dozen of the other

definitions.text: It's decisive in court in case of six of one and half-a-dozen of the other

parts.words: It's decisive in court in case of six of one and half-a-dozen of the other
parts.note: reads like a legal ruling on a draw, but the court is a tennis court and six games each in a set calls for a deciding game

explanation.surface: A judge settles a case where both sides are equally balanced.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of one and half-a-dozen of the other is an idiom for no difference; literally it is a 6-6 score in a tennis set.
explanation.definitionFit: The special deciding game played in tennis when a set reaches six games all.

clue.text: Propagated roses primarily in garden area

indicators.note: in places the initial letter inside the word for the garden plot

parts.note: a bed is an area of a garden for planting

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the initial letter of roses is used

explanation.surface: Roses were grown chiefly in one plot of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plants or animals propagated are raised or reproduced.

clue.text: Unstoppable destroyers in naval chase at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Warships that cannot be halted pursue each other across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests naval destroyers; the definition means great slides of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: Crashing masses of snow sweep away everything in their path and cannot be halted.

clue.text: Emotional release exploded in boat race

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Feelings burst out during the Oxford and Cambridge rowing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not a link: IN BOAT RACE gives the ten letters. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Psychological term for the discharge of repressed emotion by reliving an experience.

clue.text: Interrogated about old college — is education limited?

parts.note: CA is short for circa, meaning about
a tech was a technical college, a now-dated kind of British institution
education cut short gives the abbreviation ED

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a former college's teaching has been restricted.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to question someone closely and systematically, originally on religious doctrine.

clue.text: Mark boundaries between food shop and college

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone draws lines between a delicatessen and a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fix or mark the limits of something.

clue.text: Dime novel, last of tetralogy showing bottle

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of Dime are made into something new

parts.note: John is the last of the four Gospels, a set of four works

explanation.surface: A cheap pulp book, the final one in a four-part series, features a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Dime novel' as cheap fiction; 'novel' is the anagram signal turning DIME into DEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large narrow-necked bottle, often in a wicker case.

clue.text: Among his work Beethoven's fourth is arousing stuff

indicators.note: among places one letter in the middle of the work's title

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's third symphony

indicators.note: fourth picks the fourth letter of the word Beethoven's

explanation.surface: Beethoven's Fourth Symphony is said to be sexually stimulating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his work' points to the Eroica Symphony, not the Fourth; 'fourth' means the fourth letter, T, of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sexually arousing literature or art.

clue.text: Unusually pacy horse runs over rodent

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of pacy appear in an unusual order
in a down clue, runs over means the word goes backwards up the column

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: An unusually fast horse runs over a small animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest living rodent, from South America.

clue.text: Having a disease — I caught it breaking the rules

parts.note: having a disease means being ill
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone sick admits catching it by flouting regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unlawful, forbidden by law or custom.

clue.text: Comments on the side, as woman accepts drink with 9

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the other pieces go inside the name

parts.note: Maria is a woman's name
gin is a drink
9 refers to the answer at 9-across, whose first name is Al

explanation.surface: A woman takes a gin with a gangster, and remarks are made on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is a cross-reference to the gangster at 9-across, used here for his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes written in the margins of a page are comments at the side.

clue.text: Problems, first off, for foreign currency

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: trouble means problems

explanation.surface: Trouble with money abroad, first and foremost.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the currency of Russia.

clue.text: Modest about page that's written for paper

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the letter

parts.note: coy means shy or modest

explanation.surface: A shy writer of news stories puts pen to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalistic term: the written material for publication in a newspaper.

clue.text: Independent producer, for example

parts.note: reads like a freelance film maker, but the Independent is a British newspaper and this person writes material for it

explanation.surface: A freelance film maker is given as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent is a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer who produces news stories for a newspaper such as the Independent.

clue.text: Arranger, oddly enough, was composer

indicators.note: oddly says take the letters in odd positions of Arranger

explanation.surface: The music arranger had, strangely, once been a composer himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link; Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Thomas Arne, the 18th-century English composer.

clue.text: Put in position, Communist leader has moved in first

indicators.note: says the letters i-n are taken from the end of the leader's name and placed at its front

parts.note: Stalin was the Soviet Communist leader

explanation.surface: A Communist chief has moved in first and put people in their places.
explanation.walkthrough: STALIN with IN shifted to the front gives the spelling with one L, a British variant.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym (British spelling with one L): to place or set up in position.

clue.text: Ambassador left to bore one foreign capital

parts.note: HE is His or Her Excellency, the title of an ambassador
to bore a well is to sink it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An envoy is left to tire out someone from another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like 'weary'; here it means drill, as in sinking a shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the capital city of Finland.

clue.text: Confusing note with others?

parts.note: looks like a musician's error, but describes the condition of being unable to tell musical pitches apart

explanation.surface: A musician keeps muddling one note with the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to distinguish musical pitch mixes up one note with another.
